rationale: This is a mechanical product of two canonical published anomalies (earnings-to-price and the Sloan accrual measure, here in its CFO-minus-earnings form), so it rediscovers "quality-adjusted value" rather than testing a new interaction, and the rank-product construction adds no economic content beyond the two known legs.

Book-to-market interacted with gross profits-to-assets is precisely the combination Novy-Marx (2013) published and marketed as the canonical profitability-plus-value strategy, making this a direct rediscovery.

Beyond being Piotroski's positive-CFO screen applied to B/M, the INDICATOR collapses all negative-CFO firms to exactly zero, so they pool indistinguishably with genuine growth (low B/M) names in the short leg and the resulting spread is not the stated "value within cash-generating firms" comparison.

The enterprise-value construction is correctly specified and the leverage gate on EBITDA yield is a defensible, less-trodden variant than the standard B/M-times-profitability composites, though it overlaps materially with quality/safety-plus-value (QMJ) and the ratio is non-monotone for firms with negative EV or negative EBITDA, which should be handled before testing.

Sales-to-price conditioned on a five-year net-margin trend is the most substantive interaction in this batch and the expression matches the hypothesis, but the margin-improvement leg echoes Piotroski's Δmargin component and the 5-period TREND on annual data will bite into coverage and tilt toward long-lived survivors — worth checking coverage before crediting any alpha.

Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa and Nikolaev already showed that the return predictability in book-to-market comes essentially entirely from its retained-earnings component, so scaling B/M by RE/AT is a rediscovery of a documented decomposition rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.
